title: Cluster D — Shebelinka-Slovyansk P3381 vs P3382: PARTIAL_OVERLAP (one corridor, replacement-in-progress, completion status unresolved)

rows.recommendation: Do not change Status or delete. Add a ResearcherNotes entry stating: this row is the ORIGINAL 1969-built Du700 pipe on the Shebelinka(Kharkiv oblast)-Slovyansk(Donetsk oblast) corridor, currently the subject of a government-approved section-by-section replacement by a new Du500 pipe (= P3382). Per TSOU's own project documentation, the Du700 pipe is dismantled ONLY AFTER each corresponding Du500 section is commissioned -- so this row's true surviving length is presumptively LESS than 70.00 km once any replacement section is complete, but full completion status could not be verified from any public source reachable in this pass (last confirmed construction activity: 2020). Do NOT revise LengthKnown down without a source dated after the 2020 ProZorro contract confirming which UT sections have actually been decommissioned. Flag for Update: get a current (2023-2026) TSOU annual/investment report or a fresh site inspection before touching this row's length -- tsoua.com returned HTTP 403 to this pass's fetches.
rows.notes: Confirmed via 3 independent primary/near-primary sources that this row and P3382 describe ONE corridor at two points in an active, government-sanctioned rebuild, not two separately-built parallel Soviet strings: (1) Ministry of Energy and Coal Industry of Ukraine Order No.445, 12.07.2013, approving the working project 'Реконструкція газопроводу Шебелинка - Слов'янськ (заміна Ду 700 на Ду 500, км 1,1 - км 68,0; довжиною 67 км)... Ділянка УТ-5 (км 55,1 - км 68,6)', customer PJSC Ukrtransgaz -- states the reconstruction covers the FULL corridor km1.1-68.0, length 67km, i.e. essentially P3381's whole route minus the first 1.1km. (2) Nashi Groshi, 04.12.2015: Ukrtransgaz's Kharkivtransgaz branch awarded a 95.85M UAH contract (30 Nov 2015) to TOV 'Trubremont' to build a new Du500 pipe PARALLEL to the existing Du700 route over the full 67km, then tie in to the operating system -- explicit replacement methodology, target completion end-2016. (3) ProZorro/openprocurement.org public API, tender UA-2020-04-01-000023-c, 'Section UT-4 (km39.9-55.1). RESIDUAL WORKS' -- procuring entity 'Operator of the Gas Transmission System of Ukraine' (TSOU), status complete, one active contract signed 21 May 2020 for 29,657,697.56 UAH gross. This 2020 'residual works' contract is direct evidence the project had NOT finished on the original 2015-2016 schedule and was still under construction 4+ years later. A companion UT-5 2020 construction tender (title indexed as UA-2020-06-10-007174-b) and a 2019 construction-supervision tender for UT-4/UT-5 (UA-2019-09-30-000369-a) also exist per search-engine indexing of prozorro.gov.ua, but both are JS-rendered SPA pages I could not resolve to their internal API IDs within this pass's effort budget -- their content is UNVERIFIED, flagged for a follow-up pass, not treated as a dead link. No source found confirms actual physical dismantling of any Du700 stretch, nor any status update after 2020 -- this corridor sits in Kharkiv/Donetsk oblast, active front-line territory since 2022, and I found no dated evidence either way on a wartime pause. A web-search snippet suggesting an 'October 2022 restoration' of a 'reserve Shebelinka-Slovyansk' pipeline was checked and is a MISREAD -- the only fetched primary confirms it refers to a DIFFERENT line, 'Shebelinka-Novopskov', whose valves Russian occupiers illegally shut on 11 May 2022 (lb.ua, 14.05.2022); that incident does not belong to this cluster. Currently the pair double-counts length in any roll-up: 70+54=124km of pipe recorded against a corridor whose own approved design documents put its total length at ~67-68.6km -- a ~54-56km overstatement risk as long as both rows are summed as separately 'operating'.

rows.recommendation: Do not merge into P3381 and do not delete. Add a ResearcherNotes entry: this row is the NEW Du500 replacement pipe for sections UT-1 through UT-4 (km1.1-55.1, summing to the row's 54.00 km) of the Shebelinka-Slovyansk corridor, built parallel to the existing Du700 pipe (=P3381) per Ministry of Energy Order No.445 (2013) and the 2015 Ukrtransgaz/Trubremont construction contract; the two rows are lifecycle stages of ONE corridor, not independent lines. Flag as an open question for Update: the StartYear1=2022 value does not match any tender/contract/design date found (design approval 2013, main construction contract 2015 targeting end-2016, a documented 'residual works' contract for this exact section signed 21 May 2020) -- 2022 may correspond to an actual commissioning date for one or more UT sections that this pass could not source, or may be a data-entry artifact; verify against a TSOU 2021-2023 annual/investment report before treating 2022 as confirmed. Because GEM has no km-marker/segment model, recommend Update distinguish the two rows going forward via SegmentName (e.g. 'UT-1 through UT-4, km 1.1-55.1, Du500 replacement') rather than treating either as a clean duplicate to be dropped.
rows.notes: See P3381's notes for the full evidence chain (same three sources apply to both rows, since they describe one project). The section arithmetic corroborates that P3382 is specifically the UT-1..UT-4 replacement segment: the 2013 Order No.445 covers UT-5 alone (km55.1-68.6, 13.5km section length) and leaves the remaining km1.1-55.1 (=54.0km, matching P3382's LengthKnown exactly) to the other sections (UT-1..UT-4), which per the task brief's own section-tender arithmetic sum to 12.5+12.5+13.8+15.2=54.0km. A companion 2013 order for UT-4 specifically (indexed only as 'Наказ №444 від 12.07.2013' via a ligazakon.ua search snippet, dated the SAME day as the UT-5 order No.445) further corroborates the section-by-section approval scheme, but I could not independently fetch its content (ligazakon.ua redirected to a login wall) -- flagged as an unverified supporting detail, not relied upon as a load-bearing source. No source establishes P3382 as an independently-planned, permanently-parallel line in its own right (the pattern that refuted duplication in the comparable Kazakhstan cluster) -- every source found describes it exclusively as a REPLACEMENT for the corresponding Du700 stretch, with the old pipe explicitly scheduled for dismantling once the new section is commissioned. That is the basis for calling this PARTIAL_OVERLAP rather than DUPLICATE_REFUTED.

summary: GEM records the Shebelinka(Kharkiv oblast)-Slovyansk(Donetsk oblast) gas corridor as two rows with the IDENTICAL PipelineName: P3381 (70.00km, 700mm, StartYear1 1969, operating) and P3382 (54.00km, 500mm, StartYear1 2022, operating). The structural signature -- identical name, shared endpoint, one row's length (54km) matching the documented sum of four of five reconstruction sections on the other row's corridor -- reads exactly like a duplicate. Per this cluster's governing discipline, that signature is a hypothesis until sourcing decides it, and here the sourcing is unusually direct: three independent origins (a 2013 Ukrainian Ministry of Energy and Coal Industry order approving the working project; a 2015 investigative-journalism report on the resulting Ukrtransgaz construction tender; and the ProZorro procurement database's own 2020 record of a 'residual works' contract for the same project) all describe this as ONE government-sanctioned reconstruction: the original 1969 Du700 pipe is being replaced, section by section (UT-1 through UT-5, km1.1-68.0/68.6, ~67km total), by a new Du500 pipe laid parallel to the old route and then tied in -- with the old pipe explicitly scheduled for dismantling only AFTER each new section is commissioned. This is decisively different from the Soviet-era pattern of independently-operated PARALLEL strings that refuted duplication in a comparable Kazakhstan cluster: no source here describes the Du500 pipe as its own permanently-coexisting, separately-planned trunk: every source frames it as a REPLACEMENT for the specific Du700 stretch it parallels. So the verdict is neither a clean DUPLICATE_CONFIRMED (I could not verify that the old pipe over the relevant stretch has actually been removed / is factually gone) nor DUPLICATE_REFUTED (there is no independent-trunk argument here to refute it with) -- it is PARTIAL_OVERLAP: two records of the same physical corridor at different, overlapping points in an active rebuild whose completion status is unresolved. The project also plainly slipped its schedule: tendered in 2015 for end-2016 completion, it still required a construction-supervision tender in 2019 and a dedicated 'residual works' contract (signed May 2020, ~29.7M UAH) for just the UT-4 section -- meaning as of 2020, four years past the original target, the corridor was still under active construction. Nothing dated after 2020 could be sourced, and this corridor runs through active front-line Kharkiv/Donetsk territory since 2022, so the war's effect on completion (acceleration under urgency, or a multi-year pause) is genuinely unknown from public sources reached in this pass. One specific dead end is worth recording precisely: a search snippet suggested an 'October 2022 restoration' of a 'reserve Shebelinka-Slovyansk' pipeline; fetching the only available primary on this showed it actually concerns a DIFFERENT, adjacent pipeline ('Shebelinka-Novopskov', valves shut by Russian occupiers 11 May 2022) -- that claim does not belong to this cluster and should not be imported into it. Net effect for the tracker: as things stand, the pair double-counts length in any roll-up (70+54=124km recorded against a corridor whose own design documents put its total at ~67-68.6km, a ~54-56km overstatement) -- a real problem worth flagging -- but the fix is not a simple merge or a length cut to P3381, because the actual as-built/as-dismantled state past 2020 is unverified. Recommendation: ResearcherNotes on both rows recording the shared-corridor / replacement-in-progress relationship and the double-count risk, an open question flagged for Update on P3382's 2022 StartYear1, and a follow-up research task (not this pass) to chase TSOU's own post-2020 investment reporting and the two ProZorro tenders (UT-5 2020 construction; 2019 supervision) that this pass located but could not read past their JS-rendered shells.
